sections.heading: Principle
sections.body: Separate a planet's prominence from whether it is easy, difficult, dignified, or helpful. Prominence answers how loudly a planet speaks in the chart; benefit, harm, dignity, and condition answer what quality that voice carries.

sections.heading: Do Not Overload Signs
sections.body: Do not make sign placement carry the whole interpretation. A sign colors a planet, but prominence comes from placement, motion, visibility, angularity, repetition, and direct contact with chart-defining points. A weakly emphasized planet in a vivid sign can still be a side note.

sections.heading: Primary Prominence Factors
sections.body: Use several independent signals before calling a planet dominant. Angularity, stations, direct contact with the Sun or Moon, tight aspects, rulership of major chart points, and repeated thematic testimony all increase signal. The luminaries begin with natural visibility, but they still need context.

sections.heading: Factors
sections.body: These factors are weighting inputs for synthesis, not final interpretations.

items.label: angularity
items.body: Planets near the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, or IC are easier to see in the life. Angular placement raises volume and makes the planet more eventful.

items.label: station
items.body: A planet near a station can become more noticeable because its motion is emphasized. Treat station as prominence, not automatically as crisis.

items.label: solar-visibility
items.body: Relationship to the Sun matters for visibility. Combustion, under-the-beams, heliacal emergence, and cazimi should modify how clearly the planet can act.

items.label: luminary-contact
items.body: Close contact with the Sun or Moon makes a planet more personal because it shapes identity, vitality, instinct, or daily emotional pattern.

items.label: rulership-and-regard
items.body: A planet that rules, aspects, or otherwise strongly testifies to a key point may describe that point more directly than a planet with only abstract dignity points.

items.label: repetition
items.body: Treat a planet as central when its topics repeat through sign, house, aspect, rulership, and chart pattern. One indicator raises a question; repeated indicators make a through-line.

sections.heading: Use In Product
sections.body: Use prominence to decide which chart factors deserve user-facing emphasis. Do not present every planet equally. Name the loudest two or three planetary through-lines, then explain the evidence and the choice point.

sections.heading: Source Note
sections.body: Paraphrased from local review PDFs supplied June 2026: Seven Stars Astrology lessons on planetary prominence and aspects, Astrodienst Astrowiki pages for Grand Cross, Grand Trine, T-Square, Yod, and Astrodienst/Astrowiki Jones chart-pattern material. Source PDFs were reviewed locally and not copied into this repository.
